rows.evidence: Q1: Material and Methods <U+2013> four field experiments 2013-2016 at the Ushkonyr demonstration site, Kazakhstan, rice and soybean, drip with mulching film vs flooding, three replications. Q2: Abstract and Conclusions <U+2013> authors state as their own three-year finding that drip irrigation with mulching film promotes early and uniform emergence of rice and soybean shoots and intensive growth; Results text on soybean notes good early growth under the film version (Figures 8-10).
rows.notes: Emergence is reported only as a qualitative conclusion; no table or count of emergence/field viability is shown although the methods mention accounting field viability of seeds on fixed platforms. Single site; only two crops; plots 0.04-0.6 ha; no measured intermediate variable (soil temperature/moisture under film asserted, not measured); no stated conditions or limitations specific to emergence; no dispersion statistics for emergence.

rows.evidence: Q1: Material and Methods <U+2013> own multi-year field experiments with drip irrigation and mulching film on rice and soybean, weed contamination counted by a standard technique. Q2: Results (text after Table 12/Table 13) and Conclusions <U+2013> drip irrigation with mulching film reduced weed contamination of rice 8-10 times, which the authors say allows manual, mechanical and chemical weed treatments to be excluded; drip plots without film were overgrown with weeds and chemical/mechanical control was ineffective; in soybean, weeds under drip with mulch film did not exceed 36-44 plants/m2 early in the season.
rows.notes: Weed suppression is attributed by the authors to the mulching film rather than to localized wetting by drip; drip without film failed from weeds. Could be read as a condition (film required), but film is part of the DIPM technology so not counted for Q7. Single site, plot scale, no mechanism measured, no stated limitations; '8-10 times' and '36-44 units/m2' are loose ranges, not dispersion of replicates, so Q9 no.

notes: Full text appears complete. Translation quality is poor and many results (emergence, weed counts) are stated qualitatively without supporting tables. The study is on drip irrigation with plastic mulching film vs flooding/furrow, matching the DIPM technology in the passages.
